chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
He who guards his secret retains control in his own hands.

key_terms.بيده: in his hand, under his control

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of guarding one's secrets in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) links the preservation of one's secret (sir) to the preservation of one's will (ikhtiyar), a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical tradition where discretion prevents external manipulation. This teaching underscores that self-control is not merely internal but is maintained by withholding information that others could use to influence or constrain one's decisions. The principle highlights the strategic wisdom of silence in navigating social and political dynamics.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 162. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
He who guards his secrets retains control in his own hands.
